add.title: Add credential
add.staticHint: This is the password that will be stored and copied to your clipboard when you use this credential.
add.challengeHint: The shared secret used to compute HMAC signatures. Can be plain text or a base32-encoded key.
add.totpAlgoHint: Default is SHA-1. If your provider's otpauth URI specifies SHA256 or SHA512, use that value.
add.errorInvalidBase32: Secret contains invalid characters — TOTP and HOTP secrets use A-Z and 2-7 only (0, 1, and 8 are also accepted as lookalikes)

edit.title: Edit Credential
edit.description: Update the label, issuer, category, and tags for this credential.

setup.step1Subtitle: Your 2FA codes and credentials, encrypted and portable
setup.step1Description: Tegata is a portable authenticator that stores your 2FA codes and other credentials in an encrypted vault.
setup.step2Tip: 💡 Tip: Store your vault on a USB or microSD for security and portability. Install Tegata on any device to access it.
setup.onlyRemovable: Only removable drives (USB, SD, and microSD) are shown.
setup.warningBody: This path doesn't appear to be on a removable drive. For better security, store your vault on a USB or microSD card; physical separation helps keep your vault safe if your computer is compromised.
setup.step3Description: This passphrase encrypts your vault. Choose something strong and memorable.
setup.step4Warning: Store this key separately from your USB drive. It is the only way to recover your vault if you forget your passphrase.
setup.savedKey: I have saved my recovery key
setup.step5Description: Your vault has been created and encrypted. Save your recovery key somewhere safe.
setup.auditDescription: Log every authentication event to a tamper-evident ledger. Requires Docker.
setup.detectedVaults: Detected vaults on your removable drives.
setup.enterPathNoVaults: Enter the path to your vault file.
setup.errorPassTooShort: Passphrase must be at least 8 characters

settings.clipboardDescription: Clear the clipboard automatically after copying a credential.

settings.recoveryTooltip: Confirm that the recovery key you saved still matches your vault. This is the only way to regain access if you forget your passphrase.
settings.recoveryHint1: Check for typos—dashes, spaces, and letter case matter.
settings.recoveryHint2: Make sure this key is for this vault, not a different one.
settings.recoveryHint3: If you have lost your recovery key, consider changing your passphrase to something memorable while you still have access.
settings.recoveryHint4: You may also want to export your credentials as a backup.
settings.exportDescription: Enter a passphrase to encrypt the export file.
settings.errorExportTooShort: Passphrase must be at least 8 characters
